title: Quantitative Bounds for Roth's Theorem
description: Formalizes the Roth number r₃(N) — the maximum size of a 3-AP-free subset of [N] — and states the major quantitative bounds from Roth (1953) through Kelley-Meka (2023).

originalContributions: Formal definition of the Roth number r₃(N) as Finset.sup over AP-free subsets of ZMod N
Proof that r₃(N) ≤ N (upper bound from Fintype.card)
Proof that r₃(N) ≥ 1 for N ≥ 1 (singleton witness)
Proof of max_iterations_bound: density increment iteration count ≤ ⌊100/δ²⌋
Formal statements of 4 quantitative bounds: Roth, Behrend, Bloom-Sisask, Kelley-Meka

overview.historicalContext: The quantitative study of r₃(N) — the maximum size of a 3-AP-free subset of [N] — has been one of the most active areas in combinatorics for 80 years. Roth (1953) proved r₃(N) = O(N/log log N). Behrend (1946) constructed AP-free sets showing r₃(N) ≥ N·exp(-c√(log N)). After decades of incremental improvements (Bourgain, Sanders), Bloom-Sisask (2020) broke the logarithmic barrier, and Kelley-Meka (2023) achieved r₃(N) ≤ N·exp(-c(log N)^{1/12}), nearly matching Behrend.
overview.problemStatement: Define the Roth number r₃(N) = max{|A| : A ⊆ [N], A contains no 3-term AP} and formalize the known quantitative bounds.
overview.text: Formalizes the Roth number and states the progression of quantitative bounds from Roth (1953) to Kelley-Meka (2023).
overview.proofStrategy:
1. Define r₃(N) as the maximum cardinality of AP-free subsets of ZMod N using Finset.sup.
2. Prove basic properties: r₃(N) ≤ N (trivial), r₃(N) ≥ 1 (singleton witness).
3. State the density increment iteration bound: at most ⌊100/δ²⌋ increments before density exceeds 1.
4. State five quantitative bounds with precise mathematical formulations.
keyInsights: **Roth Number Definition**: r₃(N) = Finset.sup over the powerset of ZMod N filtered by APFree, applied to card. This is noncomputable but logically clean.
**Iteration Bound**: The density increment δ → δ + δ²/100 allows at most ⌊100/δ²⌋ steps. Combined with modulus decay analysis, this yields the quantitative bound.
**Behrend vs Kelley-Meka Gap**: The lower bound exp(-c√(log N)) vs upper bound exp(-c(log N)^{1/12}) leaves a significant gap. Closing this is a major open problem.

**Modulus Decay is the Key**: All upper bounds differ in how they analyze the modulus decay through density increment iterations. Roth gets √N per step, Kelley-Meka gets much better decay via Bohr sets.

sections.mathContext: $r_3(N) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z},\; A \text{ AP-free}\}$. Basic bounds: $1 \leq r_3(N) \leq N$.

sections.title: Part II: Iteration Bound from Density Increment
sections.summary: Proves max_iterations_bound and iterations_before_contradiction (0 sorries). density_upper_bound_from_iteration was removed (stated δ² ≤ 100/N, equivalent to r₃(N) ≤ 10√N, which is false by Behrend's construction).

sections.title: Part III: Quantitative Bounds
sections.summary: States four quantitative bounds: Roth O(N/log log N), Behrend Ω(N·exp(-c√log N)), Bloom-Sisask O(N/(log N)^{1+c}), Kelley-Meka O(N·exp(-c(log N)^{1/12})). All 4 sorry — deep published results requiring substantial proof infrastructure.
sections.mathContext: History of bounds: Roth (1953) → Bourgain (1999) → Sanders (2011) → Bloom-Sisask (2020) → Kelley-Meka (2023).

crossReferences.description: Extends the qualitative Roth's theorem (r₃(N) = o(N)) with quantitative bounds

conclusion.summary: Defines the Roth number r₃(N) and states the major quantitative bounds from Roth (1953) through Kelley-Meka (2023). Proves basic properties and the iteration bound from the density increment.
conclusion.implications:
This formalization provides:

1. **Formal definition of r₃(N)** for use in future quantitative additive combinatorics work.
2. **Precise statements** of the five key quantitative bounds, ready for future proof efforts.
3. **Iteration bound framework** connecting the density increment to quantitative results.
openQuestions: Can Roth's original O(N/log log N) bound be formally proved from the density increment?
Can Behrend's construction be formalized to prove the lower bound?
What infrastructure is needed for the Kelley-Meka proof?
